La notación la inventó <strong>Jan Łukas: The notation was invented by Jan Łukasiewicz around 1924, and it was neither reverse nor anything to do with machines: he was a logician, and was seeking to write logical formulas without brackets. Since he was Polish, it was called Polish notation. It was turned round, operators behind instead of in front, in the fifties, when it was seen that this way it could be evaluated with a stack on the fly; the one who put it into practice in compilers was the Australian Charles Hamblin in 1957. A notation invented for writing logic on paper turned out to be the natural way of talking to a machine that did not yet exist.
